title: Avionics Self Test 2 – Advanced (50Q)
description: Harder 50-question avionics self test (ET-AV01 to ET-AV07) with the same per-module blueprint as Self Test 1. Includes calculation and applied-concept questions with closer distractors, drawn from the AVO All Exams 2024 file.

questions.question: If the distance between two point charges is doubled, the electrostatic force between them becomes:
options: A. One half of its original value
B. One quarter of its original value
C. One eighth of its original value
questions.explanation: Coulomb's law: F ∝ 1/r². Doubling r divides the force by 2² = 4.

questions.question: A wire's length is doubled and its cross-sectional area is also doubled (same material, same temperature). Its resistance:
questions.explanation: R = ρL/A. Doubling both L and A cancels out, so R stays the same.

questions.question: A magnet that was pushed into a coil is now withdrawn. Compared with insertion, the galvanometer deflection is:
options: C. Zero, because the flux is constant
questions.explanation: By Faraday's and Lenz's laws the induced EMF reverses polarity when the flux change reverses, so the deflection reverses.

questions.question: A series circuit has R = 30 Ω and total impedance Z = 50 Ω. What is its power factor?
questions.explanation: Power factor = R/Z = 30/50 = 0.6 (lagging or leading depending on the reactance).

questions.question: In a balanced delta connection the phase current is 10 A. The line current is approximately:
questions.explanation: In a delta connection I_line = √3 × I_phase = 1.732 × 10 ≈ 17.3 A, while line voltage equals phase voltage.

questions.question: A transformer has 110 primary turns and 20 secondary turns. With 220 V applied to the primary, the secondary voltage is:
questions.explanation: Vs = Vp × Ns/Np = 220 × 20/110 = 40 V (a step-down transformer).

questions.question: Once an SCR has been triggered into conduction, it can normally be turned off by:
options: B. Reducing the anode current below the holding current
C. Applying a negative pulse to the gate only
questions.explanation: After latching, the gate loses control. The SCR turns off only when anode current falls below the holding current (or the anode is made negative).

questions.question: An inverting summing op-amp has three 1 kΩ input resistors, a 2 kΩ feedback resistor and inputs of 1 V, 2 V and 3 V. The output voltage is:
A 3-phase full-wave rectifier is fed from a 60 Hz supply. The ripple frequency at its output is:
questions.explanation: A 3-phase full-wave rectifier gives six pulses per cycle, so the ripple frequency is 6 × 60 = 360 Hz.

questions.question: Which amplifier class suffers from crossover distortion, which Class AB biasing is designed to overcome?
questions.explanation: In Class B each transistor conducts for 180° and neither conducts near zero crossing. A small forward bias (Class AB) removes the dead zone.

questions.question: The hexadecimal number 2C is equal to which octal number?
Simplify Y = [(A + B′)(C + D′)]′
questions.explanation: By De Morgan: (A + B′)′ + (C + D′)′ = A′B + C′D.

questions.question: A 4-bit binary adder adds 1111 + 1111 with carry-in 0. The result is:
questions.explanation: 15 + 15 = 30 = 11110₂, so the 4-bit sum is 1110 with a carry-out of 1.

questions.question: A 4-bit binary up-counter holds 1010. After 3 clock pulses it holds:
What is the even-parity bit for the code 1100100, and what is the resulting code word (parity bit first)?
questions.explanation: The code has three 1s (odd). An even-parity bit of 1 makes the total number of 1s four.

questions.question: Which interrupt input of the 8085 microprocessor has the highest priority?
questions.explanation: The priority order is TRAP (highest), RST 7.5, RST 6.5, RST 5.5, then INTR (lowest). TRAP is also non-maskable.

questions.question: In DO-178B software levels, a failure that prevents the crew from performing their tasks and can cause serious or fatal injuries to some occupants is classified as:
questions.explanation: Level B (Hazardous/Severe-Major) means a large reduction in safety margins or crew capability; Catastrophic (Level A) would cause loss of the aircraft.

questions.question: What distinguishes the Harvard architecture from the Von Neumann architecture?
options: A. A single shared bus for instructions and data
B. Separate buses and memories for instructions and data
questions.explanation: Harvard uses separate memories and buses for program and data, allowing simultaneous access. Von Neumann uses one shared memory and bus.

questions.question: How does armature reaction lead to brush arcing in a DC generator?
options: A. By shifting the neutral axis away from the brush position
B. By increasing the field winding resistance
C. By reducing the number of commutator segments
questions.explanation: Armature flux distorts the main field and moves the magnetic neutral plane, so the brushes short coils carrying voltage, producing sparks.

questions.question: Which combination of conditions can cause thermal runaway in a NiCad battery?
options: A. Deep discharge at low temperature
B. High battery temperature together with overcharging
C. Charging with too low a current
questions.explanation: Overcharge makes the cell generate heat, which lowers internal resistance and increases charge current, a self-reinforcing rise in temperature.

questions.question: A star-connected 3-phase generator has a line voltage of 208 V. The approximate phase voltage is:
Which parameters must be matched before paralleling AC generators?
options: A. Voltage, frequency and phase sequence
B. Current, power factor and torque
questions.explanation: Generators must have matched voltage, frequency and phase sequence (and phase angle) to avoid large circulating currents when connected.

questions.question: What is the minimum bending radius normally allowed for a wire bundle?
questions.explanation: EWIS practice sets the minimum bend radius of wire bundles at ten times the outside diameter of the bundle to avoid damage to insulation and conductors.

questions.question: Which of the following wire sizes is the largest conductor?
questions.explanation: In the AWG system a smaller gauge number is a larger conductor; 0000 (4/0) is the largest of the choices.

questions.question: Which is NOT a factor used to determine the size of a wire for an aircraft circuit?
questions.explanation: Wire size is selected for current capacity, allowable voltage drop, resistance and mechanical strength, not by insulation strength.

questions.question: A 3-phase induction motor is supplied at 50 Hz and runs at 1440 rpm. Its percentage slip is:
questions.explanation: The nearest synchronous speed (4 poles) is 1500 rpm. Slip = (1500 − 1440)/1500 = 4%.

questions.question: If both the field current direction and the armature current direction of a DC motor are reversed, the motor will:
options: A. Reverse its direction of rotation
B. Rotate in the same direction
questions.explanation: Torque ∝ flux × armature current. Reversing both reverses the product twice, so the direction is unchanged.

questions.question: A series-wound DC motor is run with no load. What is the danger?
options: A. It can accelerate to destructive speed
C. It will overheat due to high torque
questions.explanation: With no load the armature current and field flux fall, so speed rises without limit until the rotor may disintegrate.

questions.question: Cooking fires fueled by liquid cooking materials, greases and oils are classified as:
questions.explanation: Class K covers cooking oils and fats; Class C is electrical and Class D is combustible metals.

questions.question: What is a hazard of excessive use of CO₂ or other agents with a strong cooling effect on an engine fire?
options: C. Turbine housing shrinks on the turbine and may cause the engine to disintegrate
questions.explanation: Rapid cooling contracts the turbine housing onto the hot turbine wheel, which can lead to engine failure.

questions.question: Which fire detector type is most suitable for detecting rate of temperature rise?
questions.explanation: Thermocouple detectors respond to the rate of temperature rise, ignoring slow changes; thermal switches respond to a fixed temperature.

questions.question: The ratio of the maximum radiation intensity of an antenna to that of an isotropic antenna radiating the same total power is called:
questions.explanation: Directivity compares the peak radiation intensity with an isotropic reference radiating the same total power.

questions.question: The bandwidth required for single-sideband suppressed-carrier (SSB-SC) transmission is approximately:
options: B. Half that of conventional AM
C. Double that of conventional AM
questions.explanation: Conventional AM sends two sidebands (2 × fm). SSB-SC sends only one, so it needs about half the bandwidth.

questions.question: What is the fourth channel of a Cockpit Voice Recorder normally used for?
questions.explanation: A CVR records the pilot, co-pilot and third-crew channels, and the fourth channel is dedicated to the area microphone.

questions.question: An Underwater Locator Beacon (ULB) transmits a usable signal for at least:
questions.explanation: ULBs are designed to operate for 30 days after being activated by immersion in water.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of receivers (sinks) on a single ARINC 429 bus?
questions.explanation: ARINC 429 is a single-transmitter bus that supports up to 20 receivers; ARINC 629 supports up to 120 terminals.

questions.question: What is the maximum data rate of an ARINC 664 / AFDX bus?
questions.explanation: AFDX is based on full-duplex switched Ethernet at 100 Mbps; ARINC 429 is 100 kbps and ARINC 629 is 2 Mbps.

questions.question: The middle marker beacon is modulated at 1300 Hz. What color light does it illuminate?
questions.explanation: Outer marker is blue (400 Hz), middle marker amber (1300 Hz) and inner marker white (3000 Hz).

questions.question: Which ATC transponder mode allows a specific aircraft to be selectively interrogated and supports a data link?
questions.explanation: Mode S uses a unique 24-bit aircraft address for selective interrogation and includes a data-link capability, also used by TCAS coordination.

questions.question: A TCAS Resolution Advisory is typically issued about how many seconds before the closest point of approach?
questions.explanation: A Traffic Advisory comes at about 40 s and a Resolution Advisory at about 25 s before the closest point of approach.

questions.question: What is the electrical zero of a control synchro system?
questions.explanation: Torque synchros use 0° as electrical zero; control synchros use 90°, where the output voltage is nulled.

questions.question: Which synchro system uses permanent magnets in its rotors?
questions.explanation: A Magnesyn has a permanent-magnet rotor, whereas an Autosyn uses an electromagnet rotor.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of a ratiometer temperature indicator over a Wheatstone bridge indicator?
options: A. It needs no power supply
B. It uses no resistive sensor
C. It is less affected by supply voltage variations
questions.explanation: A ratiometer's deflection depends on the ratio of two currents, so changes in supply voltage largely cancel out.

questions.question: In an electrical tachometer system using a generator and a synchronous-motor indicator, the indicator responds to the generator's:
questions.explanation: The generator frequency is proportional to engine speed, and the synchronous motor indicator follows that frequency.

questions.question: Which EICAS message level requires immediate corrective action and is displayed in red?
questions.explanation: Warnings (red) demand immediate crew action; cautions are amber and advisories are white/other.

questions.question: A vertical speed indicator derives the rate of altitude change from changes in:
questions.explanation: The VSI senses the rate at which static pressure changes, using a calibrated leak between the diaphragm and the case.

questions.question: When a force is applied to a spinning gyro, the resulting movement occurs 90° from the point of application in the direction of rotation. This is called:
questions.explanation: Gyroscopic precession: the reaction to an applied force appears 90° ahead in the direction of rotor rotation.

questions.question: At which latitudes does an inertial reference unit take longer to align?
options: B. The alignment time is independent of latitude
questions.explanation: Near the poles the horizontal component of Earth's rotation is small, so gyrocompassing takes longer.

questions.question: Which type of autopilot servo moves the flight control surfaces without moving the pilot's controls?
questions.explanation: A series servo is in the control path and moves only the surface, whereas a parallel servo also moves the pilot's controls.

questions.question: On a flight director, the heading cursor is set 10° more than the actual heading. The command bar deflects toward:
questions.explanation: The steering computer commands a turn toward the selected heading, so the bar moves right to ask for a right turn.
